title: Visual Inspection
description: Visual inspection is the oldest QC check: trained eyes (sometimes aided by magnification, borescopes, or machine vision) looking for defects — cracks, discoloration, misalignment, foreign material. It catches what instruments miss and misses what instruments catch; that's why it's first, not only. Standards define lighting, viewing distance, and acceptance criteria so 'looks good' means the same thing to every inspector.

title: Dimensional Inspection
description: Dimensional inspection verifies parts match the drawing: calipers (±0.001"), micrometers (±0.0001"), CMMs (±microns), each chosen by the tolerance. The 10:1 rule — measurement uncertainty should be a tenth of the tolerance — keeps the check honest. GD&T symbols (flatness, true position) define what 'correct' means beyond simple lengths.

title: Functional Testing
description: Functional testing asks the only question the customer cares about: does it do what it's supposed to do? The unit is powered, loaded, cycled — pumps pump, apps log in, switches switch — against the specification's acceptance criteria. It catches integration failures no dimensional check can: every part in tolerance, assembly still dead.

title: AQL Sampling Inspection (ANSI/ASQ Z1.4)
description: Acceptable Quality Level sampling inspects a sample, not the lot: code letter from lot size, sample size from the letter, accept/reject numbers from the AQL. AQL 1.0 at code letter J means sample 80, accept on ≤2 defects, reject on ≥3. It balances producer and consumer risk economically — 100% inspection is often worse (inspector fatigue) and always pricier.

title: Statistical Process Control — Control Charts
description: SPC watches the process, not just the product: sample subgroups over time, plot means and ranges, and act on out-of-control signals — points beyond 3σ, runs, trends. Shewhart's insight: distinguish common-cause variation (fix the system) from special-cause (find the event). A process in control is predictable; capability indices (Cp, Cpk) say whether predictable is good enough.

title: Final Inspection

title: Calibration — Measurement Traceability
description: Calibration answers 'is the ruler right?': instruments compared against standards traceable to SI, with documented uncertainty, on schedule. ISO 17025 accredits the labs; out-of-cal tools get quarantined and their past measurements assessed. Every measurement in every QC check above rests on this one — uncalibrated instruments produce numbers, not measurements.

title: Ultrasonic Testing (NDT)
description: Ultrasonic testing finds internal flaws without cutting: high-frequency sound pulses into the material, and echoes reveal cracks, voids, and inclusions — with depth from time-of-flight. Phased-array UT steers the beam electronically, imaging welds like medical ultrasound images bodies. It inspects what the eye can't reach: pressure vessels, rails, aircraft forgings.

title: Radiographic Testing (NDT)
description: Radiography X-rays the part: dense flaws and voids show as shadows on film or digital detectors, giving a permanent image of internal quality. It sees what ultrasound can miss (volumetric flaws in complex geometry) at the cost of radiation safety controls and slower throughput. Welds in pipelines and pressure vessels are its classic beat.

title: Magnetic Particle Testing (NDT)
description: Magnetic particle inspection finds surface and near-surface cracks in ferromagnetic materials: magnetize the part, dust with iron particles, and cracks reveal themselves as particle lines where flux leaks. Fast, cheap, and sensitive — the workhorse for welds, castings, and in-service crack checks. Its limit is the material: non-ferrous alloys need penetrant instead.

title: Liquid Penetrant Testing (NDT)
description: Dye penetrant finds surface-breaking defects in anything non-porous: clean, apply penetrant, wait (dwell), remove excess, apply developer — cracks bleed red lines. Fluorescent penetrant under UV finds the finest cracks in aerospace parts. Simple, portable, and brutally honest about surface quality — the method of choice where magnetism can't go.

title: Software QA — Unit to UAT
description: Software quality climbs the test pyramid: unit tests (functions), integration (components together), system (the whole thing), acceptance/UAT (the user agrees it works). The pyramid's shape matters — many fast unit tests, few slow end-to-end — because inverted pyramids collapse under their own runtime. Coverage measures what's tested; mutation testing measures whether the tests would catch bugs.
